raw_response:
I'm 54 years old, been on this land for 25 years. Never went to school — I can't read the numbers on the fertilizer bags, but I know what they look like and how much to scoop. My husband works at the brick factory in town, so most days it's just me on the 24 mu. We have some savings from his wages, but I still watch every yuan. Last year was okay — wheat gave me about 400 jin per mu, maize around 450 jin, cotton did about 500 jin of seed cotton. Not our best year, not our worst. The neighbor Zhang Laohan tried some new wheat variety and said it was nothing special, so I'm sticking with what I know.

I keep 16 mu in wheat-maize because that's our rice bowl — steady, reliable. The other 8 mu is cotton. Cotton pays better but the picking kills my back, and with my husband gone all day, I need to hire women from the village to help. That's cash out of pocket.

For the **winter wheat** on the 16 mu, I'll plant around October 12th, same as every year. I save my own seed — no point buying what you can keep. Before planting, I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer for every 2 mu — that's roughly 25 kg per mu. Then in March at green-up, if the wheat looks yellow, I topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. Last year I only put 15 kg and the wheat was a bit thin, so this year I'll go back to 20 kg. Better to waste a little money than lose yield. I irrigate three times: once before winter freeze-up, once at jointing in April, and once at heading in May. The well water isn't free anymore — they meter it now — so I don't water if it rains. For pests, I spray herbicide once in spring and maybe insecticide if I see aphids. My nephew helps me harvest in early June with his small combine — I pay him in cigarettes and a good meal, but it's faster than doing it by hand.

For **summer maize** on the same 16 mu, the window is tight — harvest wheat, then plant maize within three or four days. I buy hybrid seed from the supply shop, about 3 jin per mu, costs me maybe 50-60 yuan. When I plant, I put compound fertilizer in the furrow — about 15 kg per mu — and spread another 15 kg of urea when the maize is knee-high. Some years I only do one topdress, but last July was dry so I'll plan for two irrigations this time, just in case. July and August, probably. I spray herbicide once right after planting, and if there are armyworms, I spray insecticide. I expect about 460 kg per mu if the rain cooperates.

For **cotton** on the 8 mu, I plant in late April. I buy improved seeds — cotton seed you can't really save, it doesn't grow right the second year. I put down base fertilizer before planting, about 20 kg of compound per mu, then side-dress urea at flowering — maybe 15 kg per mu. Cotton needs more medicine than grain. I spray for bollworm three times, and herbicide once. I irrigate twice, in July and August. Picking starts in September and goes through October — I do what I can myself, but I hire two women for about 6 days each during the peak. That's 300 yuan in wages I can't avoid. I hope for 240 kg per mu of seed cotton. The price last year was decent, so if I get that, it covers the hired labor.

Why no big changes? Because change is risky. Last year was acceptable. My neighbor who cut fertilizer to save money got 100 jin less wheat per mu — he lost more than he saved. I'd rather put a little too much urea than too little. The only thing I'm watching is the wheat seed — if the shop has that new variety everyone is talking about, maybe I'll try it on 2 mu next year. But not this year. This year, I do what I know.
